cells.tense: Right now you can see the whole picture and still pick a direction.
cells.act: claim the structure as yours in the open
cells.ask: This week, say how you see a situation and what you want done with it — out loud, before anyone asks. Once, and mean it.
cells.core: You can hold the whole picture and still choose one direction — that is what is working here. Where you decide what to do, the sight is wide and it doesn't scatter you: it lands, you name it, the room gets steadier because something has at last been said clearly. In a meeting, or with family, you are the one who says what the situation is, and others lean on it. Not because you argue — because you see. And an order comes with that. Seeing everything without picking is not the skill; the pick is, and you are allowed to make it in the open. Say the shape of it before anyone has to ask for it. A single sentence, spoken once, is the whole of this. Do it with the decision you made in private, the one waiting for permission that is not coming. Saying it is the permission. The direction was yours to set; speaking it hands the thing to people who wanted it settled.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole thing. You can pick the direction.
cells.place: where you decide what to do

cells.tense: You will still be holding all of it open a month from now.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: Stop surveying something you keep turning over. Stay with the heading you have for three days and don't re-check it.
cells.core: Every reading of a situation is being held open at once, and none of them is allowed to close. There is another possible angle, one more piece of evidence that would settle it, and a choice cannot be frozen while one more reading is still coming in. So deciding gets pushed forward: this will hold, this is the shape of it — and nothing is ever really said. The bracing eats the moment you are standing in. Deciding is not losing the other truths; it is letting one of them be the heading tonight and moving. You can be right about many things at once and still go. What you want sets the heading, not what the logic closes off. Choose one and let three days pass without turning back to look. That is not abandoning the rest. It is letting this one become real.
cells.sheetLine: You keep every door open, so nothing gets chosen.

cells.tense: You were the one who called it — and the deciding is what left.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Take the next piece of work and go halves on it with someone, start to finish. No separate version, no handing it back.
cells.core: Here is where deciding used to happen, and none of it is arriving now. The sight is still in you — you read a situation fast and correctly — but it lands and goes nowhere, because nothing is reaching the place that says this one. So the days fill with small, reversible moves, and none of them is a direction. That is not a lack of knowing. It is a lack that begins the moment a choice would commit you, and you stop. A decision needs somewhere to land to become real, and a shared one is easier to enter than a private one you have been circling. Let the next step come out of a conversation rather than out of you alone. Two streams choosing the same next move make one direction where there was none, and the sight you have gets its legs back under it.
cells.sheetLine: You can see it. Committing is what's missing.

cells.tense: You are already handing out direction and calling it circumstance.
cells.act: keep your own count of what is owed, and pay it
cells.ask: Carry a private tally this week of what you owe people and pay each one back small — the amount, the correction, the thing returned. Nobody has to see the list.
cells.core: You are steering, and if someone asked, you would say it was the situation, not you. Where you decide what to do, the calls are being made — good ones, accurate ones, early — and they are filed under things happening to you rather than choices you made. This part of you does the right thing before it has admitted it decides. That is not a fault; it is a steer that has not been claimed. The compass still works. It just does not get to hear its own voice. Do the small fair thing where only you will know it was done — money in a jar, a quiet correction, a thing returned — and hold the running sum privately. Not to build credit, but to hear the direction coming from you.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is yours. It's been filed under circumstance.
cells.place: where you decide what to do
